universal_lens: A multiagent imitation learning framework for simulating defensive trajectories in American football using deep neural networks and league-average movement patterns. Trajectory-based simulation of defensive player movements in American football using LSTM and imitation learning frameworks.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of defensive play outcomes through probabilistic pass completion models conditioned on simulated ghosted trajectories and observed player data. Bayesian inference on defensive player trajectories via probabilistic pass completion models and conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine mapping defensive state transitions via learned order-invariant models and trajectory optimization under game-theoretic constraints. Situation-aware state transitions in defensive formations modeled through multi-agent coordination and role assignment via Gaussian mixture and HMMs.

primitives.name: Defensive Trajectory Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: As defensive performance and positioning largely contribute to the overall success of the whole team, this study introduces a method to simulate defensive trajectories.
primitives.assumptions: Defensive behavior follows predictable patterns; league-average movements can be modeled via imitation learning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual player actions deviate significantly from expected positional norms.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's state transition graph where each node represents a defensive formation and edges denote movement dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Pass completion probability difference between real and simulated trajectories.

primitives.name: Multiagent Imitation Learning Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Deep neural networks are trained with a multiagent imitation learning approach, using the tracking data of players of a whole National Football League (NFL) regular season.
primitives.assumptions: Player movements are governed by shared strategic objectives and environmental constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When agent coordination fails due to insufficient training data or misaligned reward functions.

layer2.mapping: Kernel derived from pairwise interaction potentials between players in defensive formations.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of predicted movement trajectories against ground truth tracking data.

primitives.name: Ghosted Trajectory Evaluation Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: The trained pass completion probability model is used to evaluate the ghosted trajectories and serves as a metric to compare the true trajectory to the ghosted ones.
primitives.assumptions: Trajectory quality correlates with pass completion likelihood under identical conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When simulated trajectories fail to align with actual game outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic scoring function for evaluating defensive decision quality.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized deviation in pass outcome probabilities between real and ghosted paths.

primitives.name: Order-Invariant Model for Defensive Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: With the implementation of a learnable order invariant model, based on insights of molecular dynamical machine learning, the accuracy of the model is increased to 81%.
primitives.assumptions: Defensive dynamics are permutationally symmetric with respect to player identities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model parameters do not generalize across varying numbers of defenders or formations.

layer2.mapping: Kernel constructed from permutation-equivariant features of defensive player configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Model accuracy improvement over baseline non-invariant architectures.

primitives.name: Defensive Trajectory Prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Imitation learning is used to predict the trajectories of defensive players.
primitives.assumptions: Players follow deterministic motion laws; imitation learning approximates expert behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player behavior deviates significantly from training data distribution.

layer2.mapping: Maps observed defensive player positions to predicted future states using learned policy functions from imitation learning.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual trajectories.

primitives.verbatim_quote: The proposed ghosting model takes advantage of a comprehensive representation of tracking data.
primitives.assumptions: Tracking data captures full positional dynamics of all players involved.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient or noisy tracking data leads to inaccurate ghosting predictions.

primitives.name: Long-Term Dependency LSTM
primitives.verbatim_quote: LSTM layers are preferably used to model sequences of this kind and are eminently used when long-term dependencies are playing roles in current predictions.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes memory cells can retain information indefinitely; gated mechanisms prevent vanishing/exploding gradients.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Struggles with extremely long sequences (>100 timesteps); suffers from gradient saturation.

primitives.name: Least-Square Pretraining
primitives.verbatim_quote: When pretraining, the models are trained with a leastsquare learning approach without interaction of the single model itself or with other models.
primitives.assumptions: Minimizes squared error assuming independent identically distributed data; assumes linear relationship between inputs and outputs.
